title: Build a separate hub, or build Crux on top of the Claude desktop app?
context: The goal is a preview: one place to manage several agents through chat, with an orchestrator that reads their summaries, answers their questions and sends them back. The Claude desktop app's Code tab already lets one session start other sessions, receive a note when each ends a turn, and message them back. This decides how much of the plumbing you build at all.

options.name: Separate Crux hub
options.summary: Crux's own app starts the orchestrator and the agents through the Claude Agent SDK, and you chat with them there.

pros: Full control over the interface and the message flow
Not tied to any one host app
cons: You rebuild session management, permissions and transcripts
Sessions you start in a terminal or the desktop app are outside it
Weeks before you can test whether the workflow is worth it

options.name: Crux layer on the desktop app
options.summary: The orchestrator is an ordinary desktop session that starts and messages agent sessions, which the app already supports. Crux adds the summary format, the authority rules and decision cards, through the skill and optionally a side panel.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='10' y='15' width='300' height='150' rx='8' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.2' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='160' y='32' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Claude desktop app</text><rect x='30' y='45' width='80' height='105' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='70' y='101.5' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Sessions</text><rect x='120' y='45' width='175' height='50' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='207.5' y='67' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Orchestrator</text><text x='207.5' y='81' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>session</text><rect x='120' y='100' width='82' height='50' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='161' y='129' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Agent 1</text><rect x='212' y='100' width='83' height='50' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='253.5' y='129' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Crux rules</text></svg>
pros: You keep the app's chat, permissions and phone access
Testable in days: mostly skill text and a summary format
cons: Tied to the desktop app and what it exposes
Terminal sessions are not part of it
Custom interface limited to what a panel mod can do

options.name: Crux protocol, any host
options.summary: Crux defines its own messages (summary, question, reply, decision) over files and a channel server, so desktop sessions, terminal sessions and a hub interface can all join.

pros: Survives changes to any one app
cons: The most design work before anything runs
Leans on channels, still a research preview

criteria.name: Ease of reversing
criteria.note: B is mostly skill text, so little to throw away

recommendation: The point is to find out whether one place to manage agents is worth it; building on the app that already does the plumbing answers that in days, and the summary format and authority rules carry over to a separate hub later.
reason: The point is not to use the Desktop App. I want a small app with a nicer UI / UX that is more messaging-like.
